title.en: Grammar: Where the hard consonant does not double (வல்லினம் மிகா இடங்கள்)

text.en: Not every joining doubles the hard consonant; learn the exceptions.

வல்லினம் மிகா இடங்கள் are the places where the hard consonant does not double when words join. For example, in a vocative or an exclamation, in a verb followed by a noun, and when a word ends in a specific form, no doubling occurs.
Typical cases include the first-case noun followed by its verb (as in 'the bird sang' with no double), words in a series, and sentences with a vocative like 'Come, Kumar'.
Practise with pairs of sentences: one where the consonant doubles and one where it does not. Learn why the meaning changes.
